headline: Five majors under their 200-day line, greed at 69, and a whale ledger that disagrees with itself
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it is split in a telling way. BTC, ETH, XRP, and BNB all sit above their 200-day averages; DOGE and ADA sit below theirs, down 71.4% and 78.7% from their 12-month highs respectively. That is not a clean bull or bear tape, it is a market where the large-cap core has repaired its long-term trend while the second tier has not. ETH carries the only golden cross on the board (its 50-day above its 200-day), yet its MACD sits below signal, a genuine split between structure and momentum worth flagging on its own.

Momentum across the majors is warm but not manic. BTC, ETH, and SOL all cluster in the mid-to-upper 60s on RSI-14 (67.7, 67.3, 67.1), the classic zone where a trend is still climbing but has less room before it counts as stretched. BTC's MACD stays above signal and SOL's does too, both trends still confirmed by momentum. XRP and BNB show weaker RSI readings (62.0 and 63.5) with MACD below signal, trends intact by the 200-day test but losing thrust underneath. On the day, every major but ADA is red, BTC down 0.8%, ETH down 0.6%, SOL down 0.8%, yet the weekly tape mostly disagrees: SOL is up 8.8% over seven days, BTC up 1.1%, while XRP (-5.9%), BNB (-1.4%), DOGE (-10.0%), and ADA (-12.2%) are all lower on the week despite double-digit monthly gains. A single day of red says little when the windows point in different directions this often.

Positioning is where the fragility shows. BTC funding on OKX runs 0.0089% per 8 hours (9.7% annualized), ETH at 9.0% annualized, both modestly positive, meaning longs are paying shorts to stay in the trade, a cost that is normal in an uptrend but not free. The long/short account ratio tells the real story of crowding: BTC at 1.31, ETH at 1.54, SOL at 1.95, XRP at 2.66, and DOGE at an extreme 4.11 longs for every short. Open interest on BTC alone sits at $2.16B. Liquidations lean hard toward shorts getting run over almost everywhere (BTC shorts lost $566K against $67K in longs over 5 hours; SOL shorts lost $856K against $213K in longs over 5 hours), except ETH, where longs took the bigger hit ($554K versus $207K over 3 hours). A market this long-skewed with funding still positive is leverage stacked on one side of the boat, and it does not need much of a wave to matter.

Flows add a genuine contradiction rather than confirmation. ETF prints for BTC on 01 Sep 2026 show a modest $8.4M inflow, but the five-session net is $497.7M positive with same_direction_days at only 2, so the daily and the five-day windows agree on sign without agreeing on conviction. ETH's ETF flow openly disagrees with itself: an outflow of $7.4M on the day against a $600.5M net inflow over the last five sessions. Meanwhile whale wallets moved $258,975,977 net off exchanges in the last 24 hours, mostly BTC (net_usd of $258.9M same figure, since it is the only asset itemized), with $154.4M in USDC moving off Coinbase Institutional in a single transfer, an unusual size for what is meant to be a stable, low-volatility asset. That reads as dry powder being staged rather than spent. But the weekly whale ledger tells a longer story of the opposite motion: four straight weeks (ending Aug 11, Aug 18, Aug 25, and Sep 01) all show net value moving onto exchanges, $589M, $333M, $1,199M, and $211M respectively. So today's 24-hour snapshot of coins leaving exchanges sits inside a month where the dominant weekly pattern has been coins arriving on exchanges, the kind of tension that deserves naming rather than smoothing over.

Sentiment sits at 69, labeled Greed, near the top of its own 30-day range of 25 to 74. Stablecoin float is essentially flat, up just 1.09% over 30 days to $308.9B, which does not suggest a large fresh cash reserve building on the sidelines. Total market cap fell 3.87% on the day to $2.62T even as most majors show only modest daily declines, implying the drawdown concentrated outside the top names, consistent with FIL, UNI, and CRV leading gainers while TRUMP, CC, and FLR led losers, a rotation story more than a broad selloff. Worth watching from here: whether the next weekly whale print breaks the four-week onto-exchange streak, whether BTC funding or the long/short ratio (currently 1.31, richest at DOGE's 4.11) starts cooling from these long-heavy levels, and whether ETH's ETF flow settles in one direction instead of showing a positive week against a negative day.
